summary: ADD badge ships consistent with the pre-existing ticket-level ADD banner (claim verified, both bg-blue-600); suppression vs RE-FIRE correct; no hardcoded hex in diff; one polish concern: blue collides with dine_in order-type pill and yellow/amber is the kitchen 'attention' convention.

issues.problem: bg-blue-600 is a raw Tailwind utility, not a design token. The codebase exposes --color-warning (#FF9500 iOS orange) which is the conventional kitchen 'new/attention' signal (Toast/R Power use amber-family). Blue also visually collides with the dine_in ORDER_TYPE_COLORS pill at line 31 — on a dine-in ticket you get a blue 'Dine-In' header pill AND a blue 'ADD' inline badge, which dilutes the signal.
issues.suggested_fix: Either (a) re-skin both the new TicketItemRow ADD badge AND the existing ticket-level ADD banner (line 192) to bg-[var(--color-warning)] / amber-500 in a follow-up polish task, or (b) accept blue as an intentional Sear-brand signal but log a polish ticket to differentiate it from dine_in (e.g., outline ring instead of solid fill on one of them).

issues.problem: text-caption-2 is the smallest type token; on a wall-mounted KDS at arm's length the inline ADD pill may be hard to scan vs the header banner. Matches RE-FIRE pill sizing so internally consistent, but worth measuring on the actual KDS hardware.
issues.suggested_fix: Consider bumping inline badges to text-caption-1 in a future KDS legibility pass; not blocking.

benchmark_gap: Toast/R Power convention for 'new item added to existing ticket' is amber/yellow attention (matches the universal kitchen 'look here, this changed' semantic). Sear is using blue, which reads as informational/status rather than alert. Acceptable Sear-brand choice but documented gap.

summary: Premium feel achieved with proper tokens, real Tabs, EmptyState with icon+CTA, locked processor Badge, tooltipped disabled Add buttons, and zero hardcoded hex; two P2 polish gaps remain (generic skeleton bars in TerminalListTable loading state and h1 size deviates from sibling .page-title convention).

issues.problem: Hardware terminals loading state renders three plain `Skeleton h-14 w-full` bars that do not mimic the eventual 5-column table shape (Device / Mfg / Identifier / Last seen / Status pill).
issues.suggested_fix: Render skeleton rows with 5 cells of varying widths (e.g., w-32, w-40, w-44, w-20, w-20) inside a Table to match TerminalListTable's actual grid.

issues.problem: H1 uses `text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight` while sibling settings pages (kds, ai, settings root) use the `.page-title` utility (22px). Visual rhythm of settings tree drifts.
issues.suggested_fix: Replace `text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight text-foreground` with `page-title` and the description with `page-subtitle` to match siblings.

issues.problem: `border-[var(--border)]` arbitrary-value form is used in the new Discover dialog where the cleaner Tailwind v4 token utility `border-border` is available and used elsewhere in the codebase.
issues.suggested_fix: Swap `border-[var(--border)]` for `border-border` (and similarly for any other `[var(--token)]` instances introduced in this batch). Pre-existing usages in the moved WorkstationTerminalsTab are out-of-scope.

benchmark_gap: Toast and R Power empty states typically include a slightly larger hero icon (h-12 / h-16 inside a colored circle) than the EmptyState's h-8 inside p-4. Acceptance criterion #7 explicitly called for h-12 to h-16 hero size; current shared EmptyState is h-8. Not a P1 since it's a shared component used elsewhere, but worth noting for a future polish task to match Toast's emptier-states-feel-intentional standard.

summary: Offline UI is functional, premium-shaped, and Rule-18 clean; status pills, empty state, skeleton, manager-PIN gate, and 44px mobile targets all present — but every color is hardcoded hex (matches existing project pattern, so not a regression FAIL) and the spec's ask for shadcn Badge variants was implemented as custom spans.

issues.problem: StatusPill uses hardcoded hex literals bg-[#F59E0B]/10 text-[#92400E] border-[#F59E0B]/20 (and blue/red equivalents) instead of design tokens; same pattern repeats on lines 190, 217, 218, 221, 222, 245, 248, 253, 272-274, 295-297, 323, 325. Matches the established pattern in OfflineBanner.tsx and ConflictResolutionDialog.tsx so it does not regress, but the entire offline module needs a token-migration follow-up.
issues.suggested_fix: Introduce semantic tokens --color-warning, --color-info, --color-danger, --color-success in src/app/globals.css and migrate all offline/* components in a single follow-up batch. Until then accept as systemic debt.

issues.problem: Pill uses hardcoded amber/red hex (#F59E0B, #EF4444, #92400E, #991B1B) for queued vs failed states.
issues.suggested_fix: Replace with bg-warning/10 / bg-destructive/10 token classes once warning + destructive semantic tokens exist.

issues.problem: Spec asked for status pills using shadcn Badge variants; implementation uses a custom <span> with manual styling. Functionally equivalent but inconsistent with the rest of the design system.
issues.suggested_fix: Refactor StatusPill to wrap <Badge variant="warning|info|destructive"> from src/components/ui/badge.tsx — requires adding warning/info variants to the Badge component.

issues.problem: Banner dismiss X button is 28x28, under the 44x44 POS minimum (Apple HIG). This file was already this way before the batch — only the offline-state copy changed in the diff — so not a regression.
issues.suggested_fix: In a follow-up polish task bump dismiss button to min-w-11 min-h-11 with the X icon visually staying h-3.5 w-3.5 inside a larger hit target.

issues.problem: Spec said dismissible should be a chevron, not a generic X. Implementation uses lucide X icon — pre-existing pattern, not introduced by this batch.
issues.suggested_fix: If the visual change is desired, swap X for ChevronUp (collapse semantic) — but verify with Ian first since current X reads as Dismiss clearly.

benchmark_gap: Toast and R Power surface offline state in the topbar with a single colored chip + count and a dropdown; this implementation matches that pattern (chip in topbar, side-sheet drawer for detail). No competitive gap. The hex-token debt is the only premium-feel risk and matches the rest of the codebase rather than being introduced here.

summary: StaleOrderModal looks premium and follows tokens for hex, but the two CTAs use the default Button size (h-8 / 32px) which violates the POS touch-target rule (>=44x44px) for a modal that surfaces mid-service rush.

issues.problem: Refresh & discard button uses default Button size (h-8 = 32px). Spec explicitly requires touch targets >=44x44 on POS surfaces; this modal appears mid-service rush when servers tap fast.
issues.suggested_fix: Add className="touch-target h-11" (or use a size variant >=44px). Apply to both DialogFooter buttons.

issues.problem: Refresh & re-apply primary CTA uses default Button size (h-8 = 32px). Same touch-target violation as the discard button — even more critical as this is the recovery path users will reach for first.
issues.suggested_fix: Add className="touch-target h-11" or use a larger size variant. Match height of discard button so they sit aligned in the footer.

issues.problem: Uses raw Tailwind palette (bg-amber-100, text-amber-600) instead of the project semantic tokens (bg-warning-bg, text-warning) defined in globals.css. Codebase has precedent for both patterns so not a regression, but the design-token system has dedicated --warning / --warning-bg vars for exactly this iconography pattern.
issues.suggested_fix: Use bg-warning-bg + text-warning for the AlertTriangle badge so this rolls with theme/dark-mode automatically.

issues.problem: Diff rows use raw text-amber-700 and text-emerald-700 to differentiate yours-vs-server. Project has semantic --warning and --success tokens; mapping to those keeps the modal coherent with the rest of the POS palette.
issues.suggested_fix: Replace text-amber-700 with text-warning and text-emerald-700 with text-success on lines 246 and 249.

issues.problem: Diff values use truncate + title attribute. Title tooltips do not work on touch devices, so a server with a long modifier-list value cannot see the full content mid-rush.
issues.suggested_fix: Use break-words / max-h with overflow-y-auto, or expand the column to two lines max with line-clamp-2 so the value remains readable on touch.

issues.problem: DialogDescription discloses raw version numbers ("You had version 3; the latest is version 4"). Not actionable for a server and adds cognitive noise to a mid-rush dialog.
issues.suggested_fix: Move version disclosure to a small muted footer line or drop it entirely; the diff table already communicates what changed.

benchmark_gap: Toast and R Power conflict prompts use full-bleed CTAs sized for tablet thumb taps (>=48px) and lead with the action verb ("Reload order" / "Keep my changes"). Our copy "Refresh & discard" / "Refresh & re-apply" is clear but slightly long; if we keep it, the buttons must be tall enough to make the text legible at a glance from across the line.

summary: Audit log UI is clean and token-correct (no hardcoded hex, light Apple sidebar preserved), but the export PIN dialog rolls its own password input instead of reusing the canonical full-screen numpad ManagerPinDialog used everywhere else in the app, plus several spec-vs-implementation polish gaps.

issues.problem: ExportButton uses a generic shadcn Dialog + Input type=password for PIN entry. Spec explicitly requires the existing ManagerPinDialog from src/components/pos/. Every other PIN-gated action in the app (DiscountDialog, CompDialog, VoidReasonDialog, AutoGratuityBanner, StaffClockButton, PendingMutationsDrawer, TerminalDiscoveryDialog) uses ManagerPinDialog with the full-screen numpad + PIN dots. This export is the only inconsistent one — looks generic-SaaS next to the rest of the app.
issues.suggested_fix: Replace the inline Dialog with <ManagerPinDialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} title="Confirm owner PIN" description="Audit log exports require your PIN." onVerified={(managerId) => doExportWithManagerId(managerId)} />. Server side will need to accept manager_user_id or already-verified token instead of raw PIN, OR the export endpoint can verify against the verified manager_user_id pattern used elsewhere.

issues.problem: EmptyState renders without actionLabel/onAction. Spec explicitly calls for 'clear filters CTA' on the empty state, and the EmptyState component supports it via actionLabel + onAction props. User who filters to zero is stuck visually.
issues.suggested_fix: Pass clearFilters down from page.tsx and render <EmptyState ... actionLabel="Clear filters" onAction={onClearFilters} /> when hasAnyFilter is true.

issues.problem: actionVariant returns 'default' for SENSITIVE actions which renders as primary blue. Spec calls for 'sensitive amber for manager-overrides' — current rendering does not visually distinguish 'sensitive' from neutral primary, defeating the at-a-glance triage intent.
issues.suggested_fix: Either add an 'amber' / 'warning' Badge variant to the shared Badge component, or wrap with className using existing warning tokens (e.g., bg-[var(--warning-bg)] text-[var(--warning)] border-[var(--warning)]/20) — never hardcoded hex.

issues.problem: Spec calls for 'copy buttons on JSON blocks' — not implemented. StateBlock renders <pre> only, no Copy button. Owners exporting incident reports often need to paste before/after JSON into tickets.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a small ghost Button with Clipboard icon in the top-right of each StateBlock that calls navigator.clipboard.writeText(JSON.stringify(value, null, 2)).

issues.problem: Loading state shows 'Loading…' text in a single TableRow rather than skeleton rows matching the final shape. Per design rules, skeleton matching final shape is required for non-modal loading.
issues.suggested_fix: Render N skeleton rows (use existing LoadingSkeleton or ShadCN Skeleton components) shaped like the actual table rows when loading && rows.length === 0.

issues.problem: Expand chevron button is h-7 w-7 (28px) — below 44×44px touch-target minimum. Less critical for back-office than POS surface, but still flagged for tablet operators.
issues.suggested_fix: Use h-11 w-11 (44px) on touch devices, or accept that this is desktop-only back-office and document the carve-out.

issues.problem: Subtitle reads 'Every privileged action in your organization. Append-only and tenant-scoped.' — spec calls for 'Every privileged action recorded for compliance and review.' The current copy leans technical ('append-only', 'tenant-scoped') vs the spec's compliance-friendly framing.
issues.suggested_fix: Use the spec wording: 'Every privileged action recorded for compliance and review.'

issues.problem: Date inputs use type='datetime-local' which renders as the default browser control (looks different on Safari/Chrome/Firefox, generic-SaaS aesthetic). Spec calls for 'date range' which implies a unified calendar UX like the rest of premium POS competitors.
issues.suggested_fix: Replace with a shadcn DateRangePicker (Popover + Calendar) that emits ISO strings — consistent across browsers and matches the Apple iPadOS feel of the rest of the back-office.

issues.problem: ShieldCheck PIN-gated indicator uses text-emerald-600 (Tailwind utility, not a token). While not a hex literal, it bypasses the token system that the rest of the app uses (var(--primary), var(--warning), etc.).
issues.suggested_fix: Use text-[var(--success)] or text-[var(--primary)] depending on intent. Keeps theme switching coherent.

benchmark_gap: Toast and R Power both use a unified date-range picker (calendar popover) for audit/report filters rather than two datetime-local inputs. R Power's audit trail uses a side-drawer for the row detail (rather than inline expand) which preserves table density — current implementation pushes other rows down on expand. Neither competitor uses a generic password field for sensitive owner actions; both use a numpad-style PIN entry, which is exactly what Sear's existing ManagerPinDialog provides — making this export the lone outlier.

summary: The dashboard observability card uses existing card, icon, typography, spacing, and color tokens without raw hex or lying actions.
benchmark_gap: Toast/R Power expose operational health as compact owner-dashboard tiles; this follows the same dense card pattern and preserves the existing mobile dashboard layout.

summary: Error fallback screens use existing tokens, minimum touch targets, route-specific operational copy, and real reload actions.
benchmark_gap: No gap for this recovery surface; the screens follow Sear tokenized card and action patterns rather than generic default error output.

summary: Campaign wizard uses existing UI-v2 cards, inputs, badges, skeletons, empty states, icons, and tokenized colors with no raw hex or lying CTAs.
benchmark_gap: Auth-gated local render could not be visually inspected without a Supabase session, but code-level design review found no token, empty-state, touch-target, or Rule-18 violations.

summary: Settings wizard uses existing light settings layout, semantic tokens, clear checklist cards, skeleton loading, real CTAs, and responsive grid without raw hex.
benchmark_gap: No blocking Toast/R Power gap for this operational settings flow.

summary: Recovery dashboard additions keep the existing tokenized UI-v2 metric/card pattern, skeleton loading, empty states, real CTAs, and no raw hex.
benchmark_gap: Auth-gated local render could not complete without Supabase env, but production build and code review show the service recovery analytics surface follows the Toast/R Power dense backoffice metric pattern.

summary: Report-builder canvas uses tokenized UI-v2 cards, responsive dense layout, real CTAs, approval-gated AI state, and no raw hex.
benchmark_gap: Local Playwright smoke confirmed the canvas and approval panel render inside the existing reports shell; no Toast/R Power benchmark gap for this CRM builder interaction.

summary: Report builder dashboard-template panel uses existing tokens/components, has skeleton/error/empty handling, and validated at 1024x768, 1180x820, and 1366x1024.
benchmark_gap: None for this CRM backoffice extension; it keeps the existing dense reporting workflow while adding template cards with semantic demo values.
